---
title: "Curvilinear effects and mediation"
subtitle: "Example 6.1 of Mize, Doan, and Long (2019)"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

Marginal effects summarize a curvilinear relationship in a single number, and
comparing that number across a model with and without a proposed mediator tests
how much of the effect the mediator accounts for. Here income is entered with a
squared term in a linear regression of depressive symptoms; the second model
adds job satisfaction as a mediator.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/ah4_cme", clear
drop if missing(depsympB, income, inc10, age, woman, race, college, jobsat)

quietly regress depsympB c.income##c.income c.age i.woman i.race, vce(robust)
estimates store basemod

quietly regress depsympB c.income##c.income c.age i.woman i.race i.jobsat, vce(robust)
estimates store medmod
<</dd_do>>
```

The marginal effect of a one-standard-deviation increase in income in each
model, and the difference between them:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare income, models(basemod medmod) amount(sd)
<</dd_do>>
```

The **Difference** row is the part of the income effect that runs through job
satisfaction, with a standard error that accounts for the two models being
estimated on the same data. The proportion of the effect that is mediated is a
contrast between rows, so [`metest`](../../metest/index.html) can report it with
a standard error:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest (1 - 2) / 1
<</dd_do>>
```
